predecessors.note: 'carved out of southern Austrasia' by Dagobert I; 'Sometime probably between 629 and 631 Dagobert granted it as a dukedom to Gundoin.' Austrasia as a separate sub-kingdom had lapsed in 629-632 (Dagobert ruled the whole realm), so the ledger takes the land from kingdom-of-the-franks.

land.text: Alsace, divided into the Nordgau and the Sundgau; Gundoin's duchy is described as covering 'both sides of the Vosges, the Burgundian Gate, and the Transjura' (Duchy of Alsace page), but only Alsace itself is drawn

successors.note: 'the duchy of Alsace was dissolved in 742 when a successor for the deceased Duke Liutfrid was not named'; Carloman, who held Austrasia and Alemannia from 741, suppressed the Alemanni in 742-746. The ducatus 'remained a distinct unit' and was revived for Hugh, Lothair II's son, in 867 (not drawn here).

rulers.title: duke
rulers.note: Granted the dukedom between 629 and 631; the page gives no end to his rule.

rulers.name: Eticho (Adalric)
rulers.title: duke
rulers.note: The Etichonids table gives 662-690 and his death on 20 February 690; the introduction says he 'ruled from 673 to 690'. The Duchy of Alsace page does not name him.

rulers.name: Liutfrid
rulers.title: last duke
rulers.note: Bridge: the start follows Adalbert's death (722). The Duchy page: Liutfrid had died before 742 and no successor was named; the Etichonids page has a Liutfrid I as Sundgau count 747-767 and says the last Etichonid duke may have died fighting the Alemanni for Pepin the Short in the early 740s. The pages disagree.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has none; the land is inside its Kingdom of the Franks and Kingdom of Alamannia shapes). The ducatus 'corresponded to the territory of Alsace' and was first called a ducatus in the 730s; Gundoin's duchy is described as larger (both sides of the Vosges, the Burgundian Gate, the Transjura) but no later page shows the extent. Austrasia drew 623-628 and 742-751 Alsace in this batch.

ledger.note: c. 630: Dagobert I makes Alsace a dukedom for Gundoin, carving it out of southern Austrasia. 'Sometime probably between 629 and 631 Dagobert granted it as a dukedom to Gundoin'; the page dates the carving to 'the last decade of the reign of Dagobert I'. Earlier: 596 Childebert II bequeathed Alsace to Theuderic II; 610 Theudebert II forced its cession and two years later Burgundy took it back; 623 Chlothar II excluded it from Dagobert's Austrasia and was soon forced to concede it.

region.text: Alsace, divided into the Nordgau and the Sundgau; Gundoin's duchy is described as covering 'both sides of the Vosges, the Burgundian Gate, and the Transjura' (Duchy of Alsace page), but only Alsace itself is drawn

ledger.note: 742: The duchy lapses. 'The duchy of Alsace was dissolved in 742 when a successor for the deceased Duke Liutfrid was not named.' The Alemanni under Theudebald had invaded Alsace in the early 740s; Carloman suppressed them in 742-746. Alsace is the kingdom-of-austrasia dossier's 742 gain.

wars.name: Alemannic invasion of Alsace and Carloman's suppression of the Alemanni

wars.outcome: The Alemanni under Theudebald invaded Alsace in the early 740s and the last Etichonid duke may have died fighting them for Pepin the Short; the duchy was dissolved in 742 and Carloman suppressed the Alemanni in 742-746.
wars.note: The Etichonids page gives no year for the invasion. Reviewer eu-07-x: 'to' capped at 742, the duchy's end; Carloman's suppression of the Alemanni continued to 746 after the duchy lapsed.

certainty.note: A Merovingian ducatus named for Alsace; the pages name the Vosges, the Nordgau and Sundgau and the Burgundian Gate, never a frontier.

notes: Written for eu-07-x from three pages (Duchy of Alsace, Etichonids, Austrasia). Phase one only, 630-742: the page says the ducatus 'remained a distinct unit' and was revived in 867 for Hugh (Lothair II's son), attached to East Francia at Meerssen in 870, and that Charles (the Bald) was duke of Alsace, Alemannia and Rhaetia in 829-831. Those later phases are not drawn; a gap-filler may extend this dossier (rule 2: one state) from the Duchy page, the Treaty of Meerssen and the Hugh of Alsace page, whose end year the pages opened do not give. Pages disagree on the last duke (the Duchy page: Liutfrid, dead before 742; the Etichonids table: Liutfrid I of the Sundgau 747-767) and on Eticho's start (662 or 673). Capitals are empty: no page names a seat. Rulers: Gundoin has no end date. The Alsace land is inside Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks and Kingdom of Alamannia (462-731) shapes; the Frankish dossier must subtract it. The 596-612 transfers of Alsace between Burgundy and Austrasia (frankish-burgundy books a 610 loss) are before this dossier's start. Wikidata left null.
